pass_a_gloss: What therefore Jesus, that is Joshua, said to the nation when setting them down upon the holy land, these things the writing might also say to us now. And the wording holds so: now be in fear of the lord and do service to him in straightness and in justice. And it will say to us being persuaded into idol service also the next things holding so: take off from yourselves the alien gods, to whom your fathers did service in the far side of the river and in Egypt, and do service to the lord. At the start then, when you were about to be catechised, it would with reason have been said to you: and if it is not pleasing to you to do service to the lord, pick out for your own selves today to whom you will do service, whether to the gods of your fathers, those in the far side of the river, or to the gods of the Amorites, among whom you settle upon the land. And the catechist would have been saying to you: but I and my household will do service to the lord, because he is holy. But now these things have no room to be said to you; for then you spoke: may it not happen for us to abandon the lord so as to do service to other gods; the lord our God, he himself is God, who led up us and our fathers out of Egypt, and guarded us throughout on all the road on which we went. But also in the compacts about reverence for God long ago you answered those catechising you this: we too will do service to the lord, for this one is our God. If therefore the one who has stepped past compacts toward humans is someone without truce and alien to salvation, what is to be said about those who through disowning set at nothing the compacts which they laid down toward God and run back toward Satan, to whom when being baptised they bade farewell? For toward such a thing one must say the words spoken by Eli to the sons: if a man sinning sins into a man, they will also pray about him; but if he sins into the lord, who will pray about him.
pass_b_english: What Joshua said to the people when he settled them in the holy land, Scripture might now say to us as well. The passage runs like this: “Now fear the Lord and serve him in uprightness and in righteousness” (Joshua 24:14). And to us, who are being urged to worship idols, it will also say the words that follow, which run like this: “Put away the foreign gods, which your fathers served beyond the river and in Egypt, and serve the Lord” (Joshua 24:14). At the beginning, then, when you were about to be instructed in the faith, it might reasonably have been said to you: “But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve, whether the gods of your fathers who lived beyond the river or the gods of the Amorites, among whom you dwell in the land” (Joshua 24:15). And the one instructing you would have said to you: “But I and my house will serve the Lord, for he is holy” (Joshua 24:15).

But now there is no room for these words to be said to you. For then you said: “Far be it from us to forsake the Lord so as to serve other gods. The Lord our God, he is God, who brought us and our fathers up out of Egypt and kept us safe all along the way we travelled” (Joshua 24:16-17). More than that, long ago, in the covenants about godliness, you gave this answer to those who instructed you: “We too will serve the Lord, for he is our God” (Joshua 24:18). If, then, one who breaks covenants made with human beings is a man outside every truce and a stranger to salvation, what must be said of those who by denying set aside the covenants they made with God and run back to Satan, whom they renounced when they were baptized? For against such a case we must say the words Eli spoke to his sons: “If a man truly sins against a man, they will pray for him; but if he sins against the Lord, who will pray for him?” (1 Samuel 2:25).

Rendered 'Joshua': the speaker who settles the people in the holy land (Joshua 24).
